title: The full sweep finishes under four minutes on a quiet machine: decisions are tested directly and real git is kept for the git contract
description: Owner decision 2026-10-30. P143.8 and P143.10 measured the sweep throughput-bound (about 2500 slot-seconds over 8 workers, 325-327 s quiet on darwin) with about 84% of the drive suite's time in process spawn; per-call git memoisation gave about 2% each and is exhausted. Most cases in tests/test_drive_phase.py, test_commit_task_work.py, test_audit_task.py and test_close_phase.py reach a decision through a real repository and real verbs although only the decision is under test. First measure: classify every case as decision-logic (git is scenery) or git-contract, with slot-seconds per class. Then convert the decision-logic cases suite by suite to call the pure decision functions on built state, keeping a small deliberate end-to-end set. Never re-record .github/sweep-costs.json from darwin.
desiredOutcome: python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py finishes under 240 s wall on the owner's machine, quiet, twice at least 20 minutes apart; every converted case still goes red on the defect it guards; the end-to-end set names what each case proves about git.

findings.issue: The guide's opening sentence 'Where a step branches on plain values, the branch is a planner under # --- deciding a step on facts ---' and the section comment's 'So each place a step branches on plain values is a planner here' claim more than the code does. Branches on plain values still decided inline: advance's file-return arm `if stored_green(...) != _evio.STORED_HOLDS` (drive-phase.py:4301), `if tree: integrate_member(...)` (4385), kept_tree_stop / redo_patch at the top of advance, writer_wait/writer_settle, triage's review_due / filed-at-head / owed_tasks branches ahead of the advance point, drive_locked's `pending['decision'] == 'triage'` and `pending.get('task')` note_sessions branches, and sign-off. A reader told every plain-value branch is a planner would look for one that does not exist.
findings.resolution: Narrow both sentences to what is true, e.g. 'Four of the drive's branch points are planners under ...: advance's writer/scope/reviewer/gate/risk/close, the triage's advance and tail, drive_locked's stale and route, and close_task's findings/lock/route/commit/answer; the other branches (the file-return arm's stored-green check, integrate_member, kept_tree_stop, the triage's head and owed checks, sign-off) are still decided inline.' Apply the same narrowing to the comment at drive-phase.py:3910-3912.

findings.issue: No case sends the sign-off-in-advance call through main() any more. The removed sq2 was an end-to-end drive: file a clean phase review, send `next P1 --answer sign-off --reason ...`, and assert exit 0, `done`, exactly one signoff verb call, and the signedOff/landed/released did-line. sq1 is still a drive and still asserts that the dispatch PRINTS that call, but nothing sends it. sq0, sq2, sq3, sq4, sq5, sq3m and sq0m now only ask the predicates and planners: `_pending_turn('route')`, `_triage_plan('advance')`, `advance_applies`, plus `apply_phase_answer` called directly. The wiring that acts on their answer goes unexercised: route 'advance' sets ctx['advance'], drive_phase carries it to the triage point, `if sent == "advance"` applies it, and `if sent == "not-applied"` prints the triage. Read, not run: a mutation of drive-phase.py:7563 to `if reason is not None:` (apply whenever an advance was sent, ignoring the planner) would leave every remaining case green, because no kept drive sends an advance. This is the path the phase-review dispatch tells the main loop to take for every clean phase, and its one-call sign-off is the cost property sq2 pinned. Plan section 5 calls this kind of loss acceptable only when it is stated, and the outcome does not state it.
findings.resolution: Restore one end-to-end advance in e2e-signoff. Either add a second clean drive or reuse _e2e_clean's first leg. Drive with phase_review=False, call _file_phase_review, then _next(M, root, mpath, '--answer', 'sign-off', '--reason', SUMMARY). Assert exit 0, instruction DONE, one ('audit-task.py','signoff') call under _counting, the signedOff, landed and released did-events, and NOT_APPLIED absent. In the findings round, send the same advance call once after the first review is filed and assert TRIAGE, NOT_APPLIED in the print, and zero signoff calls. That covers sq3's refusal arm end to end at the cost of one `next`.

findings.issue: Several narrowed labels still claim a downstream consequence that the case does not check and that no kept drive walks. sq3/sq4 say 'so the triage is printed, noted not applied, and no sign-off runs' but check only `_triage_plan` == ('not-applied', None) and a constant's prefix. rr2 says 'and the phase review is dispatched' but checks only that nothing is marked. rr4 says 'so each is recorded once' but checks only findings_held(...) is False. sr1 says 'so sign-off dispatches a new review' but checks only owed_tasks. The case ids are the lookup keys, so a reader of a red or green line trusts these clauses.
findings.resolution: Cut each label to what its condition reads: e.g. sq3 'the advance point answers not-applied', rr2 'nothing is marked at a head with no return', rr4 'the reused return is not marked recorded', sr1 'the review filed before it owes the added task its answers'. Alternatively, assert the consequence: finding 1's fix does that for sq3/sq4.

findings.issue: This file is untouched by the diff, but the diff changed what it describes. The paragraph says 'The `sg` cases drive it over the fixture plan: ... a red phase gate never reaches `signoff`, and several findings are one `finding` call - each beside a mutant driver that breaks it.' After this diff, sg3/sg3b/sg3m (red gate) and sg4m (one `finding` call) are unit cases in us-block over run_signoff/record_findings with faked verbs. Only sg1, sg2, sg4 and sg5 still drive the fixture plan (e2e-signoff). The executor's outcome notes this drift.
findings.resolution: Rewrite the sentence. The sg1/sg2/sg4 cases drive the fixture plan: model-facing steps, the committed sign-off, several findings recorded in one `finding` call. sg3/sg3m and sg4m ask run_signoff and record_findings over faked verbs: a red phase gate never reaches `signoff`, and one call per finding is caught. Do it in the phase's docs task or a follow-up, since this task's files exclude the guide.

findings.issue: Plan section 5 requires the executor to say, for each planner arm a converted block used to reach in a drive, which kept scenario still walks it or that none does. Neither the e2e-signoff header comment nor the filed outcome lists them. These arms are now proven only on their facts, with no case showing they are reachable: a return reused at the head after lost drive state (rr), a fresh review dispatched for a task added after the review (sr), a hand-off that satisfies the triage (ht), the round-cap stop (rc1), a decline on boot/gate-coverage/breach inside a drive (db/dc/di), `leave` on a moved parent (nf2), the stalled stop (bk1), and the advance (finding 1).
findings.resolution: Add the list to the e2e-signoff header comment: each arm with 'walked by <scenario>' or 'walked by no kept scenario'. A reader deciding whether a later change needs a new drive can then see the gap without re-deriving it.

Memoise resolve_author (usage_ledger.py), _git_config_origins (_panel_viewer.py), current_branch (_id_shape.py) and _worktree_key_uncached (_journal_io.py, through _config.git_place) on a witness made of the files git reads (HEAD, config files), never a timer. Red-first in both directions for every memo: a memo that never invalidates goes red, a memo that is never used goes red. _deps.py GIT_PATH_BASE_EXEMPT rows follow any git call that moves. PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md sections of each touched module.

add: tests/test__id_shape.py: each memoised read is re-asked after the witness file changes and is not re-asked while it is unchanged

outcome.technical: ATTEMPT 2 FIX: the phase gate was red on tools/_suite.py s23, 'the live tests/ tree has no unexcused bare removal of a staged fixture'. tests/test_usage_ledger.py _author_memo_cases removed its git fixture with shutil.rmtree(root, ignore_errors=True), and Windows refuses to unlink git's read-only loose objects. It now calls _harness.remove_tree(root), the same object as _suite.remove_tree and _output.remove_tree (_suite s11), and its unused `import shutil` is gone. No exemption row was added. A grep of `git diff HEAD -- tests` for rmtree|remove_tree|os.remove|unlink found 2 added removals: that one, now fixed, and test__journal_io wk20's _harness.remove_tree(_swap), which was already the helper. test__id_shape's fixtures sit under trees that the existing _harness.remove_tree calls remove, and test__panel_viewer added no removal. The plan gate allowed the edit to tests/test_usage_ledger.py. Re-run in the task tree with `cd <tree> && python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py <file>`, one file per run, every run exit 0: tools/_suite.py 35/35; test_usage_ledger 137; test__panel_viewer 13; test__id_shape 36; test__journal_io 276; test__config 381; test__deps 254. test_drive_phase (745) and test_audit_task (1199) passed in the measured export, which is HEAD plus the attempt-1 diff; the only change since is this one removal line in test_usage_ledger.py, which neither suite imports. CHANGES (tree <home>/dev/audit-plugin/claude-plugins-P152.6, base 92c399f5, nothing committed). (1) _id_shape.current_branch: git's answer is kept per realpath(cwd) beside a witness made of the HEAD file's path and bytes. On every call the file is found by git's own discovery walk: a .git dir shaped like a git dir, the dir that a .git file's `gitdir:` line names (that pointer is read on every call), or a bare git dir. A walk that finds no repository is itself a witness, so the None outside a repository is kept until a repository appears above. An answer is kept only when it is the name the HEAD bytes spell, or None beside a detached HEAD or no HEAD. A GIT_DIR-family variable (read by reference from _config._DISCOVERY_ENV through _loader) keeps nothing. The first ask in a process still costs exactly one git process. (2) usage_ledger.resolve_author(repo_root, mode, cache=True): user.email and user.name now come from ONE `git config -z --show-origin --get-regexp '^(user\.(email|name)|include\.path|includeif\..+\.path)$'`; before, the two keys were two processes. The answer is kept per process. WITNESS: identity_env() (every GIT_ variable plus HOME, XDG_CONFIG_HOME, USER and USERNAME, by value) and file_witness() (BYTES; absent files recorded as absent) over identity_files(). identity_files covers the global, XDG and system configs where the environment puts them; for every ancestor, the .git entry and the config, config.worktree and HEAD beside it; behind a gitdir: pointer, the worktree's config.worktree, HEAD and commondir and the shared config; and every origin and include target named in git's answer. Files known before git is asked are read before AND after the question, and an answer whose files moved under it is returned but not kept. Stated limit: a system config at a build-specific path that holds no identity or include key is not watched. (3) _panel_viewer: the viewer cache token changed from stat plus a 1-second settle window to bytes through usage_ledger.file_witness, with the same before/after race check. A config written a moment ago is now kept, so _git_config_origins runs only when the token moved. _identity_env and _git_config_candidates now delegate to usage_ledger (one home). _resolve_viewer calls resolve_author(cache=False); this is labelled defensive because no case can place the one file it covers. The unused _panel_discovery import was dropped and all seven names _panel_state re-exports were kept. (4) _journal_io._worktree_key_uncached: rev-parse --git-dir --git-common-dir now goes through _config.git_place, whose witness is the identity of the top's .git entry. A project below a linked worktree's top therefore asks once per process instead of once per append; the token file is still read on every call that reaches it. (5) PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md: one sentence per touched module stating its witness, and the module map regenerated with `python3 tools/lints/_deps.py --write-map` (_id_shape gains _loader, _panel_viewer loses _panel_discovery). _deps.py: no GIT_PATH_BASE_EXEMPT row or other function-keyed row names any of the four functions (grep of tools/ for resolve_author|current_branch|_git_config_origins|_worktree_key_uncached found none), so no row moved; test__deps 254/254. CASES ADDED: test__id_shape is16b, is18-is27; test_usage_ledger am1-am10; test__panel_viewer pv1-pv4 (pv1/pv2/pv3 replace the two settle-window cases, which asserted the removed behaviour); test__journal_io wk18-wk20. RED-FIRST PROBE (<scratchpad>/probe-p1526/probe/mutations.py; table in table.txt beside it; probe exit 0). Baseline green 36/36, 276/276, 13/13, 137/137. Every row landed and went RED: B1 branch never invalidates -> is19,is20,is22,is24 (29/36); B2 never memoises -> is16b,is18,is21,is23 (32/36); B3 steering env ignored -> is26; B4 keeps what git did not agree with -> is27; A1 ledger never invalidates (files) -> am2,am4,am5,am6,am8 (130/137); A2 env ignored -> am7; A3 never memoises -> am3,am8; A4 stat token instead of bytes -> am5; A5 race check dropped -> am10; A6 include targets unwatched -> am6; A7 cache=False ignored -> am9; V1 viewer never invalidates -> in-place email case,pv2 (9/13); V2 never memoises -> the resolves-nothing case,pv1 (10/13); V3 race dropped -> pv3; V4 stat token -> pv2; W1 worktree key never memoises (direct rev-parse) -> wk18 (275/276); W2 git_place witness never invalidates -> wk20. Restored: all four suites exit 0. The first probe run showed A7 SURVIVED because am9's fixture had no kept answer standing; am9 now warms the memo first and goes red. GIT CALLS (sh shim on PATH logging every git argv with its parent pid; single runs, base = git archive HEAD, after = HEAD + final diff). test_audit_task: all git 7902 -> 6466; config --get 1083 + config --list 575 -> config --get-regexp 512 + config --list 507; symbolic-ref HEAD 799 -> 363; rev-parse --git-dir --git-common-dir 704 -> 345 (asked as --show-toplevel --git-dir --git-common-dir). test_drive_phase: all git 36155 -> 36069; symbolic-ref 525 -> 483; config 339 + 336 -> 314 + 314 (+3 --get from one other process). What is left is at the per-(process,directory) floor: each remaining repeat follows a witness change, at most 2 per pair in drive. TIME (single runs each, 10-core darwin under sibling load; every row prints its own load average, which ran 21-63). The earlier diff, before the outside-a-repository memo: audit 45 s wall / 280.3 slot-s vs base 46 / 305.0; drive 179 / 1402.5 vs 174 / 1369.0. Final diff: audit 89 / 579.3 (load 34) vs 50 / 327.1 (load 25); drive 253 / 1995.5 (load 63) vs 264 / 2080.2 (load 45). Final diff without the shim, two audit pairs: after 59 / 395.5 (load 40), base 40 / 260.7 (28), after 39 / 242.0 (21), base 56 / 352.7 (55). Wall and slot time follow load, not the change, so this machine cannot resolve the saving in time. Micro, measured once: memo hit 0.19 ms (current_branch, non-repo) and 0.32 ms (resolve_author, 39 watched files), against 20.1 ms for an uncached resolve_author at load 30. Estimate from the counts: audit_task about 15-30 slot-s, drive about 1-2 slot-s, well short of the plan's 60 s. The rest of the plan's 84 s is rev-parse --show-toplevel --git-common-dir (931 audit / 655 drive; distinct per (process,dir), so a per-directory memo cannot cut it) and --show-toplevel (451 / 710). Both are git_place/_config reads outside this task's files. DEPENDANTS: usage_ledger.py - _invariants (test__invariants 136 ok), audit-usage (calls resolve_author(project, mode); cache defaults True, compatible; test_audit_usage 182 ok), test__journal_io/test__panel_page 490/test__panel_usage 44/test__report_usage 111/test__usage_detail 54/test__usage_economics 68 ok; Attributor/_close_tail/_home/_replace_rows untouched; the hooks meter-usage/journal-writes/require-plan pass (root, mode), and their first call is now one git process where it was one or two, so journal-writes' 'costs one git config read' is now true in every case (test_meter_usage 62, test_journal_writes 154, test_require_plan 238 ok; their two-argument stubs still fit). _panel_viewer.py - _panel_state re-exports _VIEWER_CACHE, _IDENTITY_ENV, _identity_env, _git_config_origins, _git_config_candidates, _resolve_viewer and _viewer, all kept (test__panel_state 39, test_panel_server 105, test__panel_write 271 ok); _refs.py is a basename reference only (test__refs 292 ok); the guide was updated; pv4 holds _IDENTITY_ENV equal to the ledger's. _id_shape.py - _proposals (is_placeholder_phase untouched; test__proposals 58 ok); audit-task, merge-manifest and migrate-manifest get the same answers through current_branch/suffix_here (test_audit_task 1199, test_merge_manifest 34, test_migrate_manifest 97 ok). _journal_io.py - only _worktree_key_uncached's internals changed, with the same contract (test__help 79, test_close_phase 272, test_integrate_task 35, test__evidence_io 313, test__invariants 136, test__scoped_commit 81, test__tree_stamp 65, test__verdict_binding 41 ok). PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md - test__deps 254 (g1 map fence matches after --write-map), test__help, test__doctor_trail 155, test__doctor_hygiene 42, test__affected_tests 35 ok; the evals hold a basename only. Test files - .github/sweep-costs.json paths unchanged (no new suite files). One combined sweep of 33 suites exited 0 with 4569 cases. ruff and vermin -t=3.8- were clean on the touched files. OUT OF SCOPE, REFUSED BY THE PLAN GATE: plugins/audit/scripts/panel/_panel_discovery.py docstring lines 598-601 still say the viewer cache 'reuses `_settled` below by reference'; that is now false. The Edit was refused verbatim: '[require-plan] plugins/audit/scripts/panel/_panel_discovery.py is outside task P152.6 ... declared by P12.2, P85.1, P122.8-z4y, P130.8, P131.1, P131.2, P138.5-myr, a different task'. A task owning that file should replace the sentence with: the viewer's token is the bytes of the few files it watches, which needs no settle window.
outcome.descriptive: Branch, author and worktree-key reads are now kept per process on the bytes git itself reads; test_audit_task's targeted git spawns roughly halve, and wall-time gain is not measurable on this loaded machine. Attempt 2 replaces a bare rmtree of a git fixture with _harness.remove_tree.
